 ASHOK NAGAR, BELAGAVI,

 ...RESPONDENTS  (BY SMT. GIRIJA S. HIREMATH, HCGP FOR R1 & R2;

THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO ISSUE A WRIT OF CERTIORARI OR ANY OTHER WRIT OR ORDER QUASHING THE NOTICES ISSUED UNDER SECTION 17(5) OF THE KARNATAKA URBAN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY ACT BEARING BENPRA/BHUSWA/YO;SAM: 58/2013-2014 DATED 10/02/2014-VIDE ANNEXURE C PASSED BY RESPONDENT NO.2 AND THE NOTIFICATION BEARING BENPRA/BHUSWA/YO;SAM 58/2006- 07/HINDALAGA DATED 23/11/2012 PUBLISHED IN KARNATAKA GAZETTE DATED 14/02/2013 VIDE ANNEXURE-D IN SO FAR AS PETITIONERS ARE CONCERNED AND ETC.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned HCGP for respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and Sri.M.A.Huliyal, learned counsel for the respondent No.3.
2.

The petitioners are before this Court questioning the legality and validity of the notices issued under Section 17(5) of the Karnataka Urban Development Authority Act, 1987 (for short the Act,
1987), dated 10.2.2014 vide Annexure-C and notification dated 23.11.2012 published in the Karnataka Gazette dated 14.2.2013 vide Annexure-D so far as the petitioners are concerned.

3. The petitioners are the absolute owners of agricultural land bearing RS.No.110/1, situated at Hindalaga village of Balagavi taluk and district are in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the said property.
The property of the petitioner No.1 is RS.No.110/1 NC: 2024:KHC-D:9488 measuring 20 guntas, whereas the property of the petitioner No.2 is RS.No.110/1, measuring 20 guntas.

They are Nayana Rajendra Dubley vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80770543/
2 both in cultivation of the land by paying the taxes pertaining to the property regularly.
4. It is the contention of petitioners that a notification dated 14.8.2002 was issued by the respondents.

entities.text: Nayana Rajendra Dubley vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no step was taken to pursue the said notification and it was not adhered to.
Therefore, the proceedings lapsed.
Thereafter, the respondent No.3 issued paper publication on 9.1.2014 alleging that respondent No.3 initiated acquisition proceedings under Section 17 of the Act 1987.

Pursuant to which, respondent No.3 issued notice under 17(5) of the Act 1987, dated 10.2.2014 to petitioners, calling upon them to file objections within 30 days from the date of the impugned notice and respondent No.3 wrongly showed the name of earlier owner and without making proper inquiry as to who is the owner of RS.No.110/1, erroneously issued notice to erstwhile owner of RS.No.110/1.
5.

The petitioner thereafter made an inquiry with respondent No.3, obtained the copy of the gazette notification and came to know that there is an illegality committed by respondent No.3 with regard to the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and Karnataka Urban NC:
2024:KHC-D:9488 Development Authority Act by initiating the gazette notification on the 23.11.2012.
6.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that without approval of the Government, without detail scheme of development activities, without application of mind and by not implementing the scheme as per Section 15 of the Act, issued the notification, which is produced at Annexure-E.

Learned counsel further contends that in similarly placed situation one of the owners of the land, had approached this Court in WP.No.104459 of 2014 on the issuance of very same notification and that the said writ petition came to be allowed by quashing the notification.

7. It is the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that after issuance of the preliminary notification, a final notification has not been issued and so also no notices have been issued to the individual owners as contemplated under the Act 1987 and therefore, the acquisition proceedings would lapse.

He also contends that the preliminary notification was issued on 23.11.2012, till date there is no further action taken by issuing final notification or for seeking the approval of the scheme from the Government.
Therefore, the period has lapsed as within reasonable period, no final notification is issued by the authorities.

Under the circumstances, he seeks to quash the notification issued by the respondent Nos.2 and 3.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:9488 8.

Learned High Court Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents/State does not dispute the factual aspect of issuance of preliminary notification and so also the non-issuance of final notification.

However, she contends that once the notification is issued, it would not lapse and the respondent No.3 is at liberty to proceed further, initiate action and pay the compensation in accordance with law.

sentences.text: Learned counsel representing respondent No.3 also contends that the proceedings could be initiated and taken forward by the respondent as there is no time limit fixed under the Act 1987 to complete the final notification.

10. I have heard learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned HCGP for respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and also learned counsel for respondent No.3.
11.

During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the judgment in the case of C.Rangegowda V/s. State of Karnataka and others, reported in (2015)4 Kar.L.J. 64 and judgment of passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of The Special Land Acquisition Officer V/s. Shri.Arvind Narayan Kalgatagi and others in Writ Appeal No.100071/2021,
disposed of on 23.04.2024, wherein the order of quashing the notification was affirmed by the Division NC: 2024:KHC-D:9488 Bench of this Court.

entities.text: C.Rangegowda V/s. State of Karnataka and others, reported in (2015)4 Kar.L.J. 64
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition Officer V/s. Shri.Arvind Narayan Kalgatagi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 contends that they are intending to challenge the Division Bench judgment passed by this Court, which has affirmed the learned Single Judge order of quashing the notification due to lapse of the acquisition proceedings.
12. Be that as it may.

As of now, there is no challenge made to the writ appeal stated herein above,
which affirmed the order of the learned Single Judge passed by this Court, which quashed the very same notification issued by the respondent No.3-authority.

Therefore, he contends that nothing would survive for the respondent No.3 to substantiate as the said notification has been quashed and the same has attained the finality in the orders passed by the Division Bench of this Court.

13. It is also relevant to extract para No. 11 of the judgment in the case of Nitya Gopal Babashet V/s the State of Karnataka in Writ Appeal No.30044/2013 and connected appeals, whereby the Division Bench of this Court has held as under:
11.

entities.text: Nitya Gopal Babashet V/s the State of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The question that arises for consideration is whether the said time limit also equally applies to acquisition proceeding?

The Apex Court has held that in the absence of a specific provisions in these enactment, the provision contained in the Land Acquisition Act cannot be the read into the provision NC: 2024:KHC-D:9488 and such time limit cannot be prescribed, but at the same time it is held merely because no such time limit is prescribed, the Authorities cannot take their own time to complete the acquisition proceedings.
If the law do not specify the time limit within which the official acts have to be completed, it is settled law that it has to be done within a reasonable time.
In that context, the Apex Court has held that even in the absence of a specific provisions a reasonable time for issuing final notification may be taken as two years.

This Court following the aforesaid judgment in the case of SRI.H.N.SHIVANNA S/O.LATE NANJAPPA & OTHERS VS. THE STATE OF KARNATAKA AND TH ANOTHER disposed of on 20 NOVEMBER 2012 has held that even in the absence of a specific provisions, a reasonable period for issuing final notification has to be two years, though not with exact mathematical preposition.

Nayana Rajendra Dubley vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80770543/
4 14.

entities.text: Nayana Rajendra Dubley vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case on hand, as stated earlier, the preliminary notification was issued initially somewhere in the year 2002.
Due to not taking it up further, the proceedings lapsed.

Thereafter, in the year 2012, the preliminary notification was issued, which is not culminated in issuance of final notification, so also the scheme for which the property was sought to be acquired has not been implemented.
Under the circumstances, there is a time period of more than twelve years, since the preliminary notification was issued that any further action is taken by respondent Nos. 2 and 3.

Though there is no time period fixed under the Act, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that when there is no specific provision with regard to the time period provided under the Act, it is assumed that reasonable period for issuing the notification would have to be taken into consideration.
The Division Bench of this Court in para 11 as stated herein above, has held that the reasonable period for final notification would be two years.
However, the same cannot be mathematical proposition or calculation for every such case.
16. Be that as it may.

In the present facts of the case, even after twelve years, no final notification is issued and no action is initiated, therefore the question of granting any further time or providing any reprieve to the respondents would not arise as they have not initiated the final notification within reasonable time.
17. Under the circumstances, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The petition is allowed.

ii) The notification dated 23.11.2012 vide Annexure-C published in the Karnataka Gazette dated 14.2.2013 vide Annexure-D NC: 2024:KHC-D:9488 insofar as the petitioners are concerned with respect to R.S.No.110/1 is quashed.
